claims.text: The ethanol oxidation performance of Pd/Co@N-C is governed by strong catalyst-support and electronic interactions between Pd nanoparticles and the Co@N-C support.
Cobalt nanoparticles promote transformation of amorphous carbon into highly graphitic carbon.
The Co-mediated graphitic support stabilizes the catalyst against structural degradation.
Interactions at the Pd/Co@N-C interface produce an electron-deficient state in Pd.
Electron-deficient Pd optimally tunes the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The proposed electronic modification favors complete ethanol oxidation through the C1-12e pathway and suppresses incomplete oxidation.
Pd nanoparticles are well anchored on a Co-mediated, nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon support.
Reducing nitrogen dopant concentration while holding other synthesis conditions constant is the proposed controlled intervention.
The hypothesis is tested for ethanol oxidation under alkaline direct-ethanol-fuel-cell conditions.
High nitrogen content causes electron transfer from Pd to the support and thereby makes Pd electron deficient.
Lowering nitrogen content weakens the electronic interaction and produces a less electron-deficient Pd state.
A less electron-deficient Pd state shifts ethanol oxidation toward partial oxidation and reduces activity and selectivity.
The complete C1-12e pathway oxidizes ethanol to CO2 and is preferable to the C2-4e pathway.
Reducing nitrogen concentration will lower ethanol-oxidation current density.
Reducing nitrogen concentration will lower CO2 selectivity and increase incomplete oxidation products such as acetate.
The original Pd/Co@N-C catalyst exhibits high activity and durability in a direct ethanol fuel cell.
The original Pd/Co@N-C catalyst has high ethanol-oxidation selectivity because of its standard high nitrogen level.
The proposed nitrogen-mediated mechanism applies primarily under alkaline operating conditions.
The nitrogen-mediated effect may be weaker or different in acidic media or when catalyst-support interactions are altered.
